extracted.intended_audience: State environmental regulators, regulated hazardous-waste facilities in Utah, and members of the public/commenters
extracted.subtask_description: EPA direct final rule granting Utah final authorization for revisions to its RCRA hazardous waste program; includes instructions for public comment, incorporation by reference of State regulations, effect of authorization, and related administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline and effect on direct final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: This direct final rule is effective on February 21, 2025 unless the EPA receives adverse written comment by January 22, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the EPA receives any such adverse comment, it will publish a timely withdrawal of this direct final rule informing the public that the rule will not take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R08-RCRA-2024-0408; FRL-12226-02-R8 by one of the following methods: (1) Federal eRulemaking Portal (https://www.regulations.gov), (2) Email to lin.moye@epa.gov, (3) Fax (303) 312-6116 (notify EPA before faxing), (4) Mail, hand delivery or courier to Moye Lin, EPA Region 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments on regulations.gov; courier/hand deliveries accepted only during Regional Office's normal hours — call in advance to verify business hours; make special arrangements for boxed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations.gov anonymous access and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal https://www.regulations.gov website is an “anonymous access” system, which means the EPA will not know your identity or contact information unless you provide it in the body of your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit an electronic comment, the EPA recommends that you include your name and other contact information in the body of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email comments captured in public docket
rubrics_metrics.description: If you send an email comment directly to the EPA without going through https://www.regulations.gov, your email address will be automatically captured and included as part of the comment that is placed in the public docket and made available on the internet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit CBI or protected information via regs.gov or email
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit information that you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or otherwise protected through https://regulations.gov, or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA's policy is that all comments received will be included in the public docket without change and may be available online, including any personal information provided, unless the comment includes information claimed to be CBI or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic file formatting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic files should avoid the use of special characters, any form of encryption, and be free of any defects or viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the EPA cannot read your comment due to technical difficulties and cannot contact you for clarification, the EPA may not be able to consider your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No second comment period; comment now if interested
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA will not institute a second comment period on this action. Any parties interested in commenting must do so at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to comment on this action, you must do so during the comment period listed in DATES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents in the docket are listed in the https://www.regulations.gov index; although listed, some information is not publicly available (e.g., CBI or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain other material, such as copyrighted material, will be publicly available only in hard copy. Publicly available docket materials are available electronically through https://www.regulations.gov. For alternative access to docket materials, contact the person in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule use criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is publishing this rule without a prior proposal because we view this as a noncontroversial action and anticipate no adverse comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate document in the Proposed Rules section will serve as the proposed rule allowing the public an opportunity to comment; the direct final rule will be withdrawn if adverse comments are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of authorization on regulated facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility in Utah subject to RCRA will have to comply with the authorized State requirements instead of the equivalent Federal requirements in order to comply with RCRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State will continue to have enforcement responsibilities, but the EPA retains authority under RCRA sections 3007, 3008, 3013, and 7003 to conduct inspections, require tests/reports, enforce RCRA, suspend or revoke permits, and take enforcement actions after notice to and consultation with the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: State maintenance requirement for equivalence/consistency/no less stringent
rubrics_metrics.description: States which have received final authorization from the EPA under RCRA section 3006(b), 42 U.S.C. 6926(b), must maintain a hazardous waste program that is equivalent to, consistent with, and no less stringent than the Federal program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As the Federal program changes, States must change their programs and ask the EPA to authorize the changes. Most commonly, States must change their programs because of changes to the EPA's regulations in 40 CFR parts 124, 260–268, 270, 273 and 279.

rubrics_metrics.name: HSWA rule implementation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: New Federal requirements and prohibitions imposed by Federal regulations that the EPA promulgates under the authority of HSWA take effect in authorized States before they are authorized for the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, the EPA will implement those HSWA requirements and prohibitions in Utah, including issuing permits, until Utah is authorized to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program revision submission standard
rubrics_metrics.description: State program revision applications must be submitted in accordance with 40 CFR 271.21 and be a 'final complete program revision application' to seek authorization of changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On April 13, 2023, Utah submitted such an application; EPA concluded it meets statutory and regulatory requirements to qualify for final authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: What happens if adverse comments received
rubrics_metrics.description: If the EPA receives comments that oppose this authorization, we will publish a timely withdrawal in the Federal Register informing the public that this direct final rule will not take effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will address all public comments in a later Federal Register; commenters will not have another opportunity to comment on this action if adverse comments trigger withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference (IBR) approval and where to obtain IBR materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register approves the incorporation by reference of certain material listed in this direct final rule as of February 21, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of the Utah regulations incorporated by reference are available from Utah Department of Environmental Quality, 288 North 1460 West, Salt Lake City, Utah 84114-4880; phone (801) 538-6776; website: https://www.deq.utah.gov/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of State-authorized regulatory provisions (codification and appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule codifies Utah's hazardous waste management program revisions by revising 40 CFR part 272, Subpart TT—Utah, and Appendix A to part 272 to list specific Utah Administrative Code chapters and sections (by chapter/section numbers) that are incorporated by reference and are part of the authorized program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document provides an extensive mapping of Federal checklists/Federal requirements to analogous state authorities and enumerates which UAC chapters/sections are included, excluded, or reserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: State provisions not part of codification / non-federally-enforceable State-only provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain State statutory and regulatory provisions are broader in scope than the Federal program, are not part of the authorized program, are not incorporated by reference and are not federally enforceable (examples listed by UCA and UAC citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule explicitly lists related legal provisions that are State-only and not federally enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized State amendments and non-delegable provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Utah has adopted but is not authorized for certain Federal final rules; some Federal rules are not delegable to States and Utah has adopted these provisions but left authority to EPA for implementation and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule enumerates categories of rules for which Utah is not authorized and explains EPA's continued enforcement of certain Federal HSWA standards until Utah receives specific authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket and supporting documents availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule identifies the Docket ID (EPA-R08-RCRA-2024-0408) and lists supporting documents (12 listed) that are part of the docket and viewable via regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are directed to regulations.gov for the index and to contact the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT person for alternative access to docket materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment inclusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA's policy is that all comments received will be included in the public docket without change and may be available online at https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided, unless the comment includes information claimed to be CBI or otherwise protected by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should avoid submitting CBI to regs.gov or email; consider redacting or submitting CBI by other means.
